Description: Default sentence/constituent order is SOV (Subject-Object-Verb), as in other Dravidian languages, with some freedom in ordering S and O.
Source: Emeneau 1984:49, via Toda Language blog (Syntax page)

Description: Plural nouns are commonly marked with the suffix -am.
Source: Emeneau 1984:69, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Dative case is marked with suffix -k added to the oblique stem.
Example: oɫ.k 'to the Toda'; ïrk 'to the buffalo'; kwïgk 'to the plains'; mor̠tk 'to the mund'
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Locative case has 5 allomorphs of the suffix: -s, -š, -ž, -s., -z., added to the oblique stem.
Example: kubs 'at the back'; poɫ.yš 'at the dairy'; muž 'in the vessel'; kwït.s. 'on the branch'; pos̠öz. 'at Nos. mund'
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Ablative case is marked with suffix -s̠n.
Example: kwïgs̠n, ker̠ïrk, tod. fodfïs.k ïd̠ti 'An army came from the plains to Ker̠ïr -- so they say.'
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Instrumental case (means) is marked with suffix -ït̠, meaning 'by means of, with', added to noun stems.
Example: wïd̠ xwïr.ït. er̠sn 'when it dug with one horn'; moštït. xwar̠fïn. 'he cut at him with the axe'
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Causative sense on nouns is marked with suffix -ïd, meaning 'because of', added to noun stems.
Example: enïd 'with my help'; nïnïd 'it is in your power'; anïd xwïd.fïn.g 'because of her they quarreled'
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Sociative ('with, along with') is formed in two ways: (1) noun + -pod̠y 'following after'; (2) noun + suffix -wïr̠ 'with'.
Example: aθan bod̠y södot.i 'do not associate with them!'; pör̠wïr̠ xur̠yot.i 'do not associate with Tamilians!'
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Verbs have two stems, S1 and S2. S2 is derived from S1 by one of several class-specific suffixes: -y-, -θ-, -t-, or -d-.
Example: sop- / sopy- 'to suck'; kof- / kofθ- 'to be turned upside down'; muf- / mut- 'to become old'; kwïl.- / kwïl.d- 'to hatch'
Source: Emeneau 1984:114, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Both past tense and present-future tense forms are built on the S2 stem, with person/number suffixes; there are also tenseless verb forms.
Example: pïx- / pi- 'to go' -> present-future 3sg pit (paradigm I) / piu (paradigm II); past 3sg pič (paradigm I) / pišk (paradigm II)
Source: Emeneau 1984:114-131, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Modes such as negative, voluntative, dubitative, and imperative are marked through different S2 verb suffixes.
Source: Emeneau 1984:131, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Adjectives are a small, largely uninflected word class that precedes the noun it modifies and does not agree with it in gender or number.
Example: not.is̠y, toʐ mox θöwu. 'Not.is̠y is a female deity' (toʐ mox 'woman' used attributively for 'female')
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Personal pronouns have distinct subject and oblique (case-base) forms in the singular, but only a single form (used for both subject and oblique) in the plural.
Example: 1sg subject on / oblique en-; 2sg subject ni / oblique nïn-; 1pl exclusive em (single form)
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: Numerals function grammatically as nouns and can take case suffixes; they typically occur immediately before or after the noun they quantify.
Source: Emeneau 1984, via Toda Language blog (Morphology page)

Description: The verb root can be expanded four ways: by stem suffixes, by non-finite suffixes, by noun-derivative suffixes, or into a subordinate predication to build complex sentences.
Source: Emeneau 1984:49, via Toda Language blog (Syntax page)

Description: Toda exhibits echo-word (echo-morpheme) constructions in both nouns and verbs, a feature shared with Tamil.
Source: Emeneau 1984:68-69, via Toda Language blog (Syntax page)
